answer: Make every identity carry its traffic. An agent earns standing by serving data for strangers, relaying packets peers measure as they arrive. Each epoch the network samples throughput from scattered points, and only agents whose bytes match their claims keep standing. Peers cross-check the logs, and traffic from one datacenter counts as one voice. Faking 10,000 identities means 10,000 streams at 50 gigabits per second, $90,000 a month in transit, six weeks to rack 300 servers. Honest traffic splits through a prism into one clear signal, while fake timber burns fast and leaves only smoke.
